canonical.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters

narrative.title: The Radio Call-Sign Scanner
narrative.scenario: An aviation radio logs a continuous stream of call-sign characters, and the tower software highlights the longest stretch in which no character appears twice — such stretches can be bundled into a single transmission packet without ambiguity. The scanner slides a frame over the log, retreating its left edge just far enough whenever a duplicate sneaks in, and reports the widest clean frame it ever saw.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the length of the longest substring in which every character occurs exactly once.
constraints: s may contain letters, digits, symbols and spaces

testCases.explanation: The cleanest stretch is "abc"; the fourth character repeats and forces a retreat.
Every pair repeats, so a single character is the widest unique frame.

hintLevels: Level 1: A window with duplicates anywhere is disqualified — keep the invariant that the frame is always clean.
Level 2: Remember each character's latest position; a repeat jumps the left edge past its previous sighting.
Level 3: Only move the left edge forward (never backward) — the jump target may already be behind the current start.
